title: Law to pilot low-traffic neighborhoods with traffic calming
summary: This bill would require the Department of Transportation to run a two-year pilot program installing at least two types of traffic calming devices, such as speed humps or raised crosswalks, in five neighborhood areas across at least three boroughs to reduce traffic in residential streets. The department must consult local community boards on device placement and study effects on crashes, injuries, noise and complaints. It must report findings and recommendations to the Mayor and Council Speaker within six months after the pilot ends.
